### 1 — Scene
A breakfast-style meal of scrambled eggs and bacon, with broccoli and a small mixed salad.

### 2 — Vessel
A rounded-square dinner plate, approximately 26 cm across. Using a 26 cm circular equivalent:
**Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ 531 cm².**
The square shape adds some uncertainty.

### 3 — Items
Scrambled eggs, bacon, broccoli, leafy greens, cucumber, and shredded carrot. There is some sheen, but no clearly identifiable separate sauce or oil; cooking fat is included in the eggs’ energy estimate.

### 4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy
The estimated food footprints total **80%** of the plate. Volumes below are outer-envelope volumes; density is the only reduction applied.

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = volume | Density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Scrambled eggs | 29% | 154 cm² × 1.35 cm = 208 ml | 0.95 | 197 g | 170 | 335 kcal |
| Bacon | 10% | 53 cm² × 0.6 cm = 32 ml | 0.9 | 29 g | 540 | 157 kcal |
| Broccoli | 18% | 96 cm² × 2.5 cm = 239 ml | 0.6 | 143 g | 35 | 50 kcal |
| Leafy greens | 18% | 96 cm² × 3 cm = 287 ml | 0.15 | 43 g | 23 | 10 kcal |
| Cucumber | 3% | 16 cm² × 0.9 cm = 14 ml | 0.65 | 9 g | 15 | 1 kcal |
| Shredded carrot | 2% | 11 cm² × 0.5 cm = 5 ml | 0.6 | 3 g | 41 | 1 kcal |

### 8 — Sanity check
**Total: approximately 424 g and 554 kcal.** This is plausible for a mostly covered dinner plate: eggs and broccoli supply most of the weight, while bacon contributes substantial energy despite its smaller weight.
